newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangling to raise US$1.3 bln in 1996-2000.
newsitem.headline: Jiangling to raise US$1.3 bln in 1996-2000.

text.p: Jiangling Motors Corp Ltd plans to use up to US$1.3 billion in foreign exchange over the next five years to expand its core operations, an official newspaper reported on Monday.

The Securities Times said Jiangling recently set up a unit in Nanchang, the capital of China's southeastern Jiangxi province, to conduct foreign exchange financing business to help raise funds at a low cost.

The newspaper said Jiangling hoped to take advantage of U.S. automobile giant Ford Motor's global influence to raise funds required to expand and revamp Jiangling's production. It gave no further details.
Ford last year paid about US$40 million to buy 80 percent of Jiangling's issue of 174 million class B shares.

At that time, Jiangling said it had 693.214 million shares outstanding, composed of 353.240 million state shares, 174.000 million B shares, 117.600 million A shares and 48.374 million legal person shares.
The same paper last week said the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China had agreed to extend Jiangling a 200 million yuan loan to supplement the Shenzhen-listed firm's working capital.
A company spokesman, contacted by telephone, said Jiangling expects to receive 70 million yuan from the bank by the end of this year and the remaining 130 million yuan in the first quarter of 1997.
He declined to give details of the interest rate or maturity of the loan. The official said Jiangling plans to channel the 200 million yuan into production of automobile engines.
He said Jiangling's results should pick up next year, when it projects output to reach 60,000 trucks and 120,000 engines annually.
